chapter: Howard McGhee's band and bebop in LA
title: Forming McGhee's group and the Downbeat opening
summary: The first McGhee band personnel, their modern ambition as West Coast counterparts of Parker and Gillespie, and the union.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Oh yeah, because I was in the idiom more or less to my liking and my desires. Roy Milton I appreciated was beautiful, you know. But Howard McGhee, they were playing more advanced music, you know. And I'm a youngster. I'm eager to play with something more advanced. Like, we were the counterparts to Charlie Parker and Dizzy Gillespie; they were on the East Coast and we were out here, you know, when we put our thing together.

So we put the group together. We had Stanley Morgan playing the guitar, and a very fine pianist, Vernon Biddle, playing the piano, and a drummer named Monk McVey (Nathaniel McVey, who was playing the drums), and Bob Kesterson(?) was the bassist. And we had rehearsed and worked on the music and everything, and... Our first job with the band was the Downbeat Club on 42nd and Central.

Right, my favorite! And we had a great engagement in the Downbeat Club there. And it wasn't too long after that... Well, I'm already in the union and everything now, and I had made a good rapport with Mister Paul Howard, who was the secretary at the Union, and Elmer Fain, he was a delegate, and... I had some fine people. Miss Florence Cadrez; she was assistant to Mister Paul Howard. And right next door to the union (I'd like to get this in) was Lee Young... The Young family lived next door to the union there on Central Avenue.
